title: Nature and Significance of Management
summary: Management is the process of getting things done through others effectively and efficiently to achieve organisational goals. This chapter covers its characteristics, objectives, importance, nature as science, art and profession, the levels and functions of management, and coordination as the essence of management.

notes.heading: Meaning of Management: Effectiveness and Efficiency
notes.html:
Management is a process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently.

  • Effectiveness = doing the right task, completing activities and achieving goals on time. It is concerned with the end result.
  • Efficiency = doing the task correctly at minimum cost; getting maximum output from minimum input. It is concerned with cost-benefit (use of resources).
BasisEffectivenessEfficiency
MeaningCompleting work on timeCompleting work at minimum cost
FocusEnd result / targetResources used
ConcernDoing the right thingsDoing things right
ExampleProducing 1,000 units by the deadlineProducing 1,000 units with less wastage of material

Memory aid: Effectiveness = Ends; Efficiency = Economy of resources. A good manager balances both.

notes.heading: Characteristics of Management
notes.html:
1. Goal-oriented process – it unites the efforts of people to achieve predetermined goals.
  2. All-pervasive – needed in all organisations (economic, social, political) and in all countries.
  3. Multi-dimensional – covers management of work, management of people and management of operations.
  4. Continuous process – planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling are performed again and again.
  5. Group activity – an organisation is a group of individuals with different needs working towards common goals.
  6. Dynamic function – it adapts to changes in the business environment.
  7. Intangible force – it cannot be seen but its presence is felt in the way the organisation functions (orderly work, targets met, satisfied employees).

Memory aid: GAM-CGDI – Goal-oriented, All-pervasive, Multi-dimensional, Continuous, Group activity, Dynamic, Intangible.

notes.heading: Objectives of Management
notes.html:
• Organisational objectives – (i) Survival: earning enough revenue to cover costs; (ii) Profit: covers cost and risk, needed for growth; (iii) Growth: expansion measured by sales, number of employees, products, capital investment.
  • Social objectives – creating benefit for society: environment-friendly methods, employment to disadvantaged sections, schools and hospitals, quality products at fair prices.
  • Personal objectives – meeting the financial needs (competitive salary), social needs (recognition) and higher-level needs (personal growth) of employees, and reconciling them with organisational goals.

notes.heading: Importance of Management
notes.html:
1. Helps in achieving group goals – gives a common direction to individual efforts.
  2. Increases efficiency – reduces cost and increases productivity through better planning, organising and control.
  3. Creates a dynamic organisation – helps people adapt to change so the firm keeps its competitive edge.
  4. Helps in achieving personal objectives – through motivation and leadership, members achieve personal goals while contributing to organisational goals.
  5. Helps in the development of society – quality goods, employment, adoption of new technology, growth and development.

notes.heading: Nature of Management: Science, Art or Profession
notes.html:
BasisFeatureDoes management satisfy it?
ScienceSystematic body of knowledge; principles based on experimentation; universal validityPartly. It has a systematic body of knowledge, but its principles deal with human behaviour, so results are not exact. It is an inexact (soft) science.
ArtExistence of theoretical knowledge; personalised application; based on practice and creativityYes, fully. Managers apply knowledge in their own personal style and improve with practice.
ProfessionWell-defined body of knowledge; restricted entry; professional association; ethical code; service motivePartly. It has a body of knowledge and associations like AIMA, but entry is not restricted by law, membership is not compulsory and the code of conduct is not binding.

Conclusion: Management has features of both science and art; it is not a full-fledged profession.

notes.heading: Levels of Management
notes.html:
Levels form the hierarchy of superior–subordinate relationships, showing authority and responsibility.

  • Top level (Chairman, CEO, MD, Board of Directors) – integrates diverse elements, frames overall objectives and strategies, is responsible for the welfare and survival of the organisation, and analyses the business environment.
  • Middle level (divisional heads, production/marketing/finance managers) – interprets policies of top management, ensures the department has necessary personnel, assigns duties, motivates and cooperates with other departments.
  • Supervisory / operational level (foremen, supervisors) – directly oversees workers, maintains quality and output, minimises wastage, ensures safety, is the link between workers and middle management.

notes.heading: Functions of Management
notes.html:
1. Planning – deciding in advance what to do and how to do it.
  2. Organising – assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources.
  3. Staffing – finding the right people for the right job.
  4. Directing – leading, influencing, motivating and supervising employees.
  5. Controlling – monitoring performance against plans and taking corrective action.

Memory aid: POSDC – Please Organise Staff, Direct and Control.

notes.heading: Coordination: The Essence of Management
notes.html:
Coordination is the process by which a manager synchronises the activities of different departments to achieve unity of action. It is not a separate function; it is the force that binds all functions.

Characteristics:

  • Integrates group efforts – gives a common focus to individual efforts.
  • Ensures unity of action – keeps all departments moving towards common goals.
  • Continuous process – begins with planning and continues till controlling.
  • All-pervasive function – needed at all levels and in all departments.
  • Responsibility of all managers – top, middle and lower level managers all coordinate.
  • Deliberate function – a manager has to make conscious efforts; cooperation alone is not enough.

Importance (why coordination is needed):

  • Growth in size – more people with individual goals need to be aligned.
  • Functional differentiation – departments tend to work in isolation (e.g. production vs sales).
  • Specialisation – specialists rely on their own judgement and may ignore others.

mcqs.q: A shoe company produced its target of 5,000 pairs on time but spent 20% more on leather than budgeted because of careless cutting. The company was:
mcqs.explanation: The target was met on time, so it was effective; but resources were wasted, so it was not efficient.

mcqs.q: Which characteristic of management is highlighted when we say that management is needed in a hospital, a school, a political party and a business firm alike?
mcqs.explanation: Management being required in all types of organisations shows that it is all-pervasive.

mcqs.q: Rekha, CEO of a textile company, studies changes in government policy and consumer tastes to frame long-term strategy. She belongs to which level of management?
mcqs.explanation: Analysing the environment and framing overall strategy is the job of top management.

mcqs.q: Providing employment opportunities to the differently-abled is which objective of management?
mcqs.explanation: Creating benefits for disadvantaged sections of society is a social objective.

mcqs.q: Management is considered an inexact science because:
options: It has no body of knowledge
Its principles deal with human behaviour, which cannot be predicted accurately
mcqs.explanation: Management principles are developed through observation but are applied to human beings, so results vary; hence it is a soft or inexact science.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a profession that management fully satisfies?
mcqs.explanation: Anyone can be appointed a manager without a specific degree or licence, so restricted entry is not satisfied.

mcqs.q: The production manager of a firm wants to manufacture a wide range of products, while the sales manager wants to sell only fast-moving items. Which need for coordination does this reflect?
mcqs.explanation: Departments with their own objectives pulling in different directions is functional differentiation, which creates the need for coordination.

mcqs.q:
Assertion (A): Coordination is the essence of management.
Reason (R): Coordination is a separate function performed only by top management.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: A is true. R is false: coordination is not a separate function and is the responsibility of managers at all levels.

mcqs.q: A supervisor at a bottling plant ensures that workers follow safety rules and that broken bottles are minimised. This shows the role of:
mcqs.explanation: Ensuring safety, quality and minimum wastage on the shop floor is the job of supervisory management.

mcqs.q: Management of work, people and operations together show that management is:

Assertion (A): Management is an art.
Reason (R): Every manager applies acquired knowledge in a personalised and creative manner.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false
mcqs.explanation: Personalised, creative application of knowledge is the key feature of an art, so R correctly explains A.

mcqs.q: A company redesigned its product line quickly when customers shifted to online buying. Which characteristic of management is shown?
mcqs.explanation: Adapting to changes in the environment shows that management is a dynamic function.

questions.answerHtml: Efficiency means doing the task correctly with the minimum cost, i.e. obtaining maximum output from the given resources.

questions.q: Why is coordination called the essence of management?
questions.answerHtml: Because it is needed in every function and at every level of management to synchronise individual and departmental efforts towards common goals.

questions.q: Explain any three organisational objectives of management.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Survival – the business must earn enough revenue to cover its costs to stay in existence.
  2. Profit – profit is necessary to cover costs and risks and to finance future activities.
  3. Growth – the business should grow in sales, number of employees, products and capital to remain competitive.

questions.q: Management is a continuous process and an intangible force. Explain these two characteristics.
questions.answerHtml:
• Continuous process – the functions of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling are performed simultaneously and repeatedly by all managers; the process never ends.
  • Intangible force – management cannot be seen or touched, but its presence is felt in the orderly functioning of the organisation, achievement of targets and satisfied employees.

questions.q: 'Management is a profession.' Do you agree? Give reasons by examining any four features of a profession.
questions.answerHtml:
No, management does not fully satisfy the features of a profession.

  1. Well-defined body of knowledge – satisfied; management is taught in colleges and institutes.
  2. Restricted entry – not satisfied; no specific degree is legally required to become a manager.
  3. Professional association – partly satisfied; bodies like AIMA exist, but membership is not compulsory.
  4. Ethical code – not fully satisfied; AIMA has a code of conduct, but it is not binding on managers.

Hence management has some features of a profession but is not a full-fledged profession.

questions.q: Distinguish between effectiveness and efficiency on any four bases.
questions.answerHtml:
BasisEffectivenessEfficiency
MeaningCompleting the task on timeCompleting the task with minimum cost
FocusEnd resultUse of resources
ConcernDoing the right thingDoing things right
MeasurementGoal achieved or notRatio of output to input

questions.q: Kavya Foods Ltd. makes ready-to-eat meals. Its CEO, Mr. Arora, decided to enter the frozen-food market. The purchase manager, Ms. Nandini, and the plant head, Mr. Jaspal, prepared departmental plans, appointed the required staff and assigned duties. Supervisor Tarun guides 40 workers on the packing line and ensures daily output and hygiene. Identify the levels of management in the case and state two functions of each level.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Top level – Mr. Arora (CEO)

  • Frames overall objectives and strategies, e.g. entering the frozen-food market.
  • Analyses the business environment and is responsible for the survival and welfare of the organisation.

2. Middle level – Ms. Nandini and Mr. Jaspal

  • Interpret the policies of top management and prepare departmental plans.
  • Ensure their departments have the necessary personnel and assign duties to them.

3. Supervisory level – Tarun

  • Directly oversees workers and maintains the quality and quantity of output.
  • Ensures safety and hygiene and acts as a link between workers and middle management.

1. Integrates group efforts – it unifies the diverse interests of individuals into purposeful work activity.
  2. Ensures unity of action – it acts as a binding force between departments so that all work towards common goals.
  3. Continuous process – it begins at the planning stage and continues till controlling.
  4. All-pervasive function – it is required in all departments and at all levels because activities are interdependent.
  5. Responsibility of all managers – top managers coordinate overall plans, middle managers coordinate departments and supervisors coordinate workers.
  6. Deliberate function – a manager must consciously coordinate; even where people are willing to cooperate, coordination gives that cooperation a direction.
